data.name: ITGA2 (Integrin alpha-2)
data.description: Integrin subunit alpha-2. Two separate findings in this Atlas: kynurenic acid from tumor microbiota induces ITGA2 upstream of an mTOR-dependent cascade that is inhibited, not activated, which sustains cathepsin V and suppresses CD8+ T cells (REN2026); and, in a different setting, collagen I signalling through alpha2beta1 integrin activates mTORC1/S6 and sustains amino-acid supply via LAT1-4F2hc (NAZ2026). The two point in opposite directions and must not be merged.
data.description_beginner: A protein on the cell surface, part of an integrin receptor. In gastric cancer, kynurenic acid from tumor bacteria switches it on, and an mTOR signal downstream of it goes down rather than up, which helps the tumor resist immunotherapy. In a different situation, the same receptor reading collagen outside the cell switches mTORC1 on instead. Same protein, opposite directions, two different settings.

studies.title: Streptococcus anginosus-associated kynurenic acid drives PD-1 blockade resistance through an ITGA2-mTOR-CTSV axis in gastric cancer.
studies.authors: Ren Y; Yu X; Jiang J; Luo J; Zhao C; Mao X; Xi Y; He J; Yu C; Hu Y

evidence.label: Animal model

studies.finding: Tumor microbiota-derived kynurenic acid drives resistance to PD-1 blockade in gastric cancer through the ITGA2-mTOR-CTSV axis: kynurenic acid induces ITGA2 and inhibits an mTOR-dependent cascade, which sustains cathepsin V expression and suppresses CD8+ T cell cytotoxic function.

studies.title: Collagen I promotes cancer cell survival via amino acid import and mTORC1/S6 activation
studies.authors: Nazemi M; Yanes B; Vancauwenberghe E; Oyelade I; Walker H; Rainero E

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: Human breast and pancreatic cancer cell lines (2D/3D culture)
studies.finding: Collagen I drives alpha2beta1 integrin-dependent mTORC1/S6 activation and membrane localization of the LAT1-4F2hc amino acid transporter, sustaining essential amino acid supply and cancer cell survival in nutrient-poor, collagen-rich tumor stroma; LAT1-4F2hc is upregulated in basal-like breast/pancreatic tumors and correlates with poor prognosis.
